title: Halabos na hipon
intro: Whole shrimp cooked in a covered pan with just salt and a splash of water until the shells turn red and the juices reduce to a salty glaze. Sweet, simple and best peeled at the table and dipped in garlicky vinegar.

steps.text: Rinse the shrimp and trim the antennae and legs with kitchen scissors, leaving the heads and shells on. Drain well.
Stir the vinegar, garlic, chili and a pinch each of salt and pepper together in a small bowl and set aside.
Spread the shrimp in a wide pan, sprinkle with the salt and pour in the water. Cover and cook over medium-high heat, shaking the pan once, until the shells turn orange-red.
Uncover and keep cooking, tossing often, until the liquid has almost cooked away and the shrimp look glossy. Stir in the butter, if using, in the last minute.
Serve hot with the vinegar dip and steamed rice.

tips: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the liquid is nearly gone. Past that point the shrimp shrink, stick to the shells and turn dry.
